{{Quote|Both sides want to use Brentaal to show that Endor was a fluke, and that they've recovered.''"
"''And Brentaal IV is the key to the Bormea sector, which we want because Mon Mothma's homeworld Chandrila is here.|Wedge Antilles and Avan Beruss|[[X-Wing Rogue Squadron 22|''X-Wing Rogue Squadron'' 22]]}} '''Brentaal IV''', known more commonly as '''Brentaal''', was a [[Planet/Legends|planet]] in the [[Brentaal system/Legends|Brentaal system]] of the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds's]] [[Bormea sector/Legends|Bormea sector]] and one that occupied what was arguably the most valuable location in the entire [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]]: the intersection of the [[Hydian Way/Legends|Hydian Way]] and the [[Perlemian Trade Route/Legends|Perlemian Trade Route]], two of the galaxy's major [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlanes]]. The fourth planet in orbit around the [[Star/Legends|star]] [[Brenta]], Brentaal had two [[Moon/Legends|moons]] and was located in the [[Ringali Shell]], a string of [[Star system/Legends|star systems]] along the Perlemian that were near the [[Ringali Nebula/Legends|Ringali Nebula]]. An arid world with warm and temperate weather, Brentaal featured two large polar caps and an equator marked by deserts and steaming oceans; most of the planet's available land was dominated by warehouses, cargo holding facilities, commerce exchanges, and other trade-related structures. Brentaal's capital of [[Cormond]] and its [[Trade Hall]] were the seat of power on the planet, with the hundreds of [[Brentaal Houses]]—the influential families that ran the planet's trade guilds—represented the citizens in Brentaal's democratic government. As a result of its location along the Perlemian Trade Route, Brentaal was a major commerce hub that became an economic power when it joined the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] sometime before [[22,000 BBY/Legends|22,000 BBY]], as it served as a checkpoint for traffic entering the Republic along the Perlemian. A [[Brentaalan]] [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] [[Scout/Legends|scout]] named [[Freia Kallea/Legends|Freia Kallea]] further bolstered her homeworld's affluence and economic power when she charted the Hydian Way around [[3700 BBY/Legends|3700 BBY]], making Brentaal the only planet to sit at the intersection of two galactic superhighways. Brentaal's economic importance made it a frequent target of military conquests; conflicts such as the [[New Sith Wars]], the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], and the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]] all saw the planet become a [[Battle of Brentaal IV (New Sith Wars)|battleground]] [[Battle of Brentaal IV (Clone Wars)|at]] [[Battle of Brentaal IV (Galactic Civil War)|least]] [[Battle of Brentaal IV (Yuuzhan Vong War)|once]] as various governments and factions fought to control Brentaal's vital hyperspace junction. ==Description== {{Quote|If Shogar Tok's insurrection is allowed to succeed, we may lose access to the Perlemian Trade Route. Access from here to the Tion Cluster will be impeded.|Plo Koon, on Brentaal IV's strategic importance|}} The fourth [[Planet/Legends|planet]] in orbit around the [[Star/Legends|star]] [[Brenta]] in the [[Brentaal system/Legends|Brentaal system]] of the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]]' [[Bormea sector/Legends|Bormea sector]], Brentaal IV was often called simply Brentaal. Brentaal IV lay in the [[Ringali Shell]], a string of [[Star system/Legends|star systems]] along the [[Perlemian Trade Route/Legends|Perlemian Trade Route]] that took its name from the nearby violet-[[Color/Legends|colored]] [[Ringali Nebula/Legends|Ringali Nebula]] that lit up the nighttime skies of planets in the region. A terrestrial world with a temperate but arid climate and two [[Moon/Legends|moons]], Brentaal occupied one of the most valuable locations in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]—the intersection of the Perlemian and the [[Hydian Way/Legends|Hydian Way]], two of the galaxy's major [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlanes]]. Brentaal's northern and southern poles were marked by large ice caps, and the rest of the planet was dominated by a chain of particularly salty [[Ocean/Legends|seas]] that separated Brentaal's eight continents. The planet had a rotational period of 23 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|standard]] [[Standard hour/Legends|hours]] and an orbital period of 342 [[Standard day/Legends|standard days]], and a diameter of 11,242 [[Kilometer/Legends|kilometers]]. [[File:Brentaal_above.png|thumb|left|250px|Starfighters fly along the surface of one of Brentaal's moons.]] The [[Commenor Run/Legends|Commenor Run]] was another hyperlane that terminated at Brentaal, linking the world with [[Caamas/Legends|Caamas]], [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]], [[Kattada/Legends|Kattada]], and [[Commenor/Legends|Commenor]]. A number of [[Space station/Legends|space stations]] orbited the planet, including a dozen or so [[XQ2 Platform]]s that were built by [[Bengel Shipbuilders]] decades before [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]].{{DoD|The Traitor's Gambit}} A dry and relatively young planet, Brentaal featured a large number of mountain ranges that had been raised by [[Groundquake/Legends|groundquakes]] and volcanic activity, and most of the planet's volcanoes were dormant by the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic's]] founding. The planet's weather was largely warm and temperate, though the equatorial band featured deserts and steaming oceans. Most of the planet's settlements were located in valleys, canyons, and deltas in the livable bands between the two ice caps and the equatorial regions, and they suffered from frequent overcrowding, though the planet's spaceports and storage facilities were primarily built atop flattened mountains. Brentaal's original colonists largely erased the planet's native flora and fauna over the course of many generations, replacing them with ecological systems found on other Core Worlds. One of the few native species to survive was the [[kundril]], a massive, multisegmented flying insect that lacked [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] and hunted by sound. A number of variations of kundril existed, with most hunting fish and seagoing mammals in Brentaal's seas, and most of the land-based kundrils were wiped out by the planet's inhabitants over the decades. The large amphibians known as [[Scrange/Legends|scranges]], native to the planet [[Dagobah/Legends|Dagobah]], could also be found in Brentaal's sewers. Air pollution was once a major concern on Brentaal, but the environmental damage was largely repaired, and the planet's air was made safe again, though it smelled slightly of [[Methane/Legends|methane]]. ==History== ===Early history=== The region around Brentaal IV, like much of the northeastern and eastern sections of the Core Worlds, was largely explored between the [[Standard year/Legends|years]] [[27,500 BBY|27,500]] and [[25,000 BBY/Legends|25,000 BBY]]. Brentaal was a member world of the Galactic Republic by the year [[22,000 BBY/Legends|22,000 BBY]], developing into a major economic hub as it served as a checkpoint for traffic entering the Bormea sector along the Perlemian during the Republic's early [[Standard century/Legends|centuries]]. Around [[24,500 BBY]], Brentaal was the site of a [[Battle of Brentaal IV (First Great Schism)|battle]] between the [[Legions of Lettow]] and the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] during the [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-using]] Order's [[First Great Schism]]. For several thousand years, the planet served as a jumping-off point for ships exploring the [[Colonies/Legends|Colonies]] region, and most of the goods that returned to the early Republic from the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] passed through Brentaal. Besides the Perlemian Trade Route, the [[Brentaal–Denon Route]] was an early hyperlane that linked Brentaal IV with the planet [[Denon/Legends|Denon]] in the southern [[Inner Rim/Legends|Inner Rim]], and the [[Corsin Run]] spiralled northeast from Brentaal to the planet [[Corsin/Legends|Corsin]] in the [[Expansion Region/Legends|Expansion Region]]. Even early in Brentaal's history, the planet was controlled by the [[Brentaal Houses]]—merchant families that competed for control of the planet's trade and shipping industries. During the [[Manderon Period]], [[Andel Tanner]] was a prominent inventor who worked on Brentaal IV around [[6000 BBY/Legends|6000 BBY]], crafting a pair of [[Slugthrower/Legends|slugthrowers]] that were valued at over 12.4 million [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] by the year [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]].{{JournalCite|4|Galaxywide NewsNets}} Around that same time, the [[Antarian Rangers/Legends|Antarian Rangers]], a group of individuals who aided the Jedi Order, established a division on Brentaal.''[[Hero's Guide]]'' Around [[4000 BBY/Legends|4000 BBY]], a number of Humans from Brentaal colonized the planet [[Muzara]] in the [[Expansion Region/Legends|Expansion Region]], barely avoiding conflict with the native [[Muza]]; the [[Brentaal League]] hoped that its settlement would make Muzara into a profitable [[Agriworld/Legends|agriworld]].''[[Tales of the Jedi Companion]]'' [[File:Hydian_Brentaal.png|thumb|right|270px|Brentaal, at the intersection of the Perlemian and the pre-existing Corsin Run and Brentaal-Denon Route]] In [[3705 BBY/Legends|3705 BBY]], [[Brentaalan]] native [[Freia Kallea/Legends|Freia Kallea]]—a daughter of [[House Kallea]] whose parents disapproved of her apprenticeship in the [[Brentaal Spacefarers League]]—began to work as a [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] [[Scout/Legends|scout]]. Over the course of the next [[3704 BBY|year]], Kallea linked together a number of pre-existing hyperlanes in the northern galaxy: the Corsin Run, [[Mandalorian Road]], [[Sprizen End Run]], the [[Spurs of Celanon/Legends|Spurs of Celanon]], and the [[Morellian Trail]]. By [[3694 BBY]], Kallea had extended the Brentaal-Denon Route all the way to the southern rim of the galaxy, forming the super hyperlane that she named the Hydian Way, after her [[Duros/Legends|Duros]] friend [[Banu Hydia]]. The events of Kallea's trailblazing, along with the Brentaal noble [[Sival Brentioch]]'s courting of Kallea during those years, were dramatized around [[1500 BBY]] in ''[[The Kallea Cycle]]'', a famous opera that endured for hundreds of years. The [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Satele Shan]], the descendant of the famous [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Revan/Legends|Revan]] and [[Bastila Shan]], was born on Brentaal IV in [[3699 BBY]], and the Jedi Knight [[Ardun Kothe]] worked with war [[Refugee/Legends|refugees]] on Brentaal during the [[Great Galactic War]] between the Republic and the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]].''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic Encyclopedia]]'' The planet was the site of a [[Republic Military/Legends|Republic Military]] [[Brentaal IV outpost|outpost]] during the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]] between the Republic and the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]] over fifty years later. That outpost was later [[Attack on the Brentaal IV outpost|wiped out]] by the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Kavos]], who [[Death/Legends|killed]] the experienced [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]] [[Ayesho]] and [[Nil (Jedi)|Nil]] in the process. During the Cold War, an anarchist group known as the [[Revolutionary Edge Brigade]] was active on Brentaal, and the group—including a [[Rattataki/Legends|Rattataki]] named [[Kaliyo Djannis]]—frequently robbed banks, blew up public holorelays, and kidnapped influential corporate and political figures. One such attack on Curovao became known as the [[Curovao Bombing]]. During the [[New Sith Wars]], a series of conflicts between the Republic and various [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] factions that spanned the millennium between [[2000 BBY/Legends|2000 BBY]] and [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]], the Bormea sector was conquered by the [[Brotherhood of Darkness/Legends|Brotherhood of Darkness]] in the year [[1002 BBY]]. Brentaal IV was [[Battle of Brentaal IV (New Sith Wars)|captured]] by the Sith shortly after Corulag and Chandrila, with the planet's defenders only offering what the Sith Lord [[Skere Kaan]] considered to be token resistance. Kaan's capture of Brentaal forced his Jedi counterpart Lord [[Hoth (Jedi Lord)|Hoth]] to make his move and draw the Sith into battle at the planet [[Ruusan/Legends|Ruusan]].''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'' ===Unrest and the rise of the Empire=== {{Quote|So—the Republic has control of the planet again. Who's going to run it?''"
"''I don't know. I imagine that's something Supreme Chancellor Palpatine will decide.|Quinlan Vos and Agen Kolar, after the Battle of Brentaal IV|}} Brentaal was the intended target of a [[Episode I Adventures 1: Search for the Lost Jedi|foiled acquisition attempt]] by [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]] in 33 BBY, when the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] boldly attempted—via machinations between the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]], [[Groodo]] the Hutt, and [[Trinkatta Starships]] of [[Esseles/Legends|Esseles]] in the adjacent [[Darpa sector/Legends|Darpa sector]]—to seize this strategic cross-roads planet, that the Federation might utterly control two major [[Hyperspace route/Legends|galactic trade routes]], the Perlemian and the Hydian Way. A team of Jedi Knights led by [[Adi Gallia/Legends|Adi Gallia]] and [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]], including [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], ultimately struck down the violent plot with its intended use against Brentaal of 50 [[Vulture-class starfighter/Legends|''Vulture''-class droid starfighters]] modified with prototype [[Hyperdrive/Legends|''hyperdrive'' engines]] branded as illegal by the Republic.''[[Episode I Adventures 1: Search for the Lost Jedi]]'' In [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], the [[Allied Tion Historical Society]]'s [[Cradle of the Galaxy]] exhibit began a Core Worlds tour on Ralltiir on 13:4:1, and the exhibit was showcased in the [[Cormond Museum of Arts]] on Brentaal starting on 14:3:1, almost a [[21 BBY/Legends|year later]], before it moved on to Chandrila two months later. On 13:4:25, the Jedi Knight [[Reeft]] was involved in an altercation in a marketplace on Brentaal; Reeft had been pursuing the thief [[Rotar Lopani]], who had allegedly stolen sensitive diplomatic [[Datapad/Legends|datapads]] from Coruscant a month earlier, but the [[Xexto/Legends|Xexto]] [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Tosinqas]] attempted to claim the 8,000-credit bounty on Lopani. Tosinqas fell several stories to land on Lopani, killing him, but the Xexto was startled by the sound of Reeft's [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] igniting and charged the Jedi only to kill himself by running into the weapon.{{HoloNetNewsWeb|53|jediwatch/13425_2.html|Three-Way Hunt Ends with Two Dead}} [[File:Battle_of_Brentaal.jpg|thumb|left|300px|The Battle of Brentaal IV]] The [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] between the Republic and the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] erupted with the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|First Battle of Geonosis]] in 13:5,''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' and unrest soon reached Brentaal when the Separatist [[Commander/Legends|Commander]] and Brentaal clan leader [[Shogar Tok]] captured a prison facility on Brentaal and converted it into his base of operations. Becoming a [[Warlord/Legends|warlord]] on his homeworld, Tok rallied his fellow [[Brentaalan]]s against what he claimed to be a corrupt Republic and establishing a Separatist military presence on the planet as early as 13:8. As part of the Jedi Knight [[Quinlan Vos/Legends|Quinlan Vos's]] deep-cover mission to infiltrate the the ranks of the [[Dark Acolyte/Legends|Dark Acolytes]], the servants of the Confederacy's [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]], the [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Tholme/Legends|Tholme]] sent Vos to Brentaal.''[[Jedi: Mace Windu]]'' Vos infiltrated Tok's prison base as "Korto Vos," and in 13:10 Vos sent a false message[[Republic 54|''Republic'' 54]] to the Republic claiming that Tok's rebel movement was unprepared for an attack. As a result, the Republic sent a fleet under the [[Jedi General/Legends|Jedi Generals]] [[Shaak Ti/Legends|Shaak Ti]], [[Agen Kolar/Legends|Agen Kolar]], [[Shon Kon Ray]], and [[Plo Koon/Legends|Plo Koon]] to drive out the Separatist presence there, but they found their enemy ready for the attack. Unable to [[Orbital bombardment/Legends|bombard]] Tok's fortress on account of its heavy shielding, the Republic tried to land ground troops to take the fortress, but the building's [[Ion pulse cannon/Legends|ion pulse cannons]] took out a large number of the Republic's [[Low Altitude Assault Transport/infantry/Legends|LAAT/i]] gunships. Kon Ray was [[Death/Legends|killed]] in the early fighting, and the Republic lost more than a quarter of their forces in the first few hours of the [[Battle of Brentaal IV (Clone Wars)|Battle of Brentaal IV]] against the natives and the [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droids]] of the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]].''[[Yoda: Dark Rendezvous]]'' Shaak Ti and her troops rescued Vos and three other former prisoners—[[Sagoro Autem]], [[Lyshaa]], and [[Ryyk (Wookiee)|Ryyk]]—and convinced them to help infiltrate Tok's fortress in exchange for their freedom. While Kolar led a diversionary attack, Ti and her group infiltrated the structure through the sewers and split up to achieve their objectives of disabling the shields and cannons and capturing Tok, and Plo Koon withdrew the Republic forces to wait for Ti's signal. Ti's group was successful in all of their objectives, though Ti was forced to kill Tok, and the Republic quickly achieved victory. During the early Clone Wars, Brentaal was represented in the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] by the Human [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Arcel Mosbree]], who planned to retire from the Senate in [[21 BBY/Legends|21 BBY]]. After the conflict on Brentaal, a Republic government was installed with [[Jerrod Maclain]] as temporary governor, as Mosbree was considered an accomplice to the Separatist movement on Brentaal and removed from office. In 14:9, [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] Palpatine formally appointed Maclain as regional governor of Brentaal, a role which Malcain filled for almost twenty-five years.{{InsiderCite|70|CIS Shadowfeed Dispatch 14:9:15 Edition}} The [[Shoosha family]] escaped from Brentaal during the battle, and the young musician [[Bann Shoosha]] composed a work entitled the [[Vissëncant Variations|Vissencant Variations]] to celebrate their escape shortly afterwards. By [[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]], the Variations were considered to be one of the great musical works of the recent millennium, despite being less than two years old.''[[MedStar II: Jedi Healer]]'' ===Under the Empire=== {{Quote|We have taken every precaution to ensure visitors enjoy their stay on Brentaal. ''The Kallea Cycle'' is an important part of this planet's—and indeed the Core Worlds'—culture. We want to avoid having anyone's experience marred by the activities of criminal elements.|Inspector Zanza Gata|}} [[File:Platt_dreaming.jpg|thumb|right|250px|A young Platt Okeefe watches starships land on Brentaal.]] The Clone Wars came to an end in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], when Chancellor Palpatine declared himself [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] and reformed the Republic as the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. In the months after the end of the Clone Wars, several agents of the former Senator [[Bail Prestor Organa/Legends|Bail Organa]] fled to [[Sel Zonn Station]], one of the XQ2 Platforms orbiting Brentaal, and Imperial agents pursued them there to prevent them from escaping and reaching Organa. Sel Zonn Station was minorly popular among some Brentaal nobles at the time, though the station had not flourished in the last few years. The famous Brentaalan smuggler [[Platt Okeefe/Legends|Platt Okeefe]] was born to [[House Okeefe]] around [[18 BBY/Legends|18 BBY]] on Brentaal,The combined evidence of ''[[Platt's Starport Guide]]'' and ''[[Platt's Smugglers Guide]]'' indicates that she was just sixteen when she received her captain's license, although the document, issued in [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]], claims that she was twenty. though she later left her homeworld to become a pilot in her teens.''[[Platt's Smugglers Guide]]'' By the year 0 ABY, the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Shettora]] operated a [[Shettora's criminal faction|criminal faction]] on Brentaal, controlling the [[Black market/Legends|black market]] on the world and selling good-quality merchandise at only slightly higher prices than normal. The Hutt [[Puullo]] served at the group's forefront, using his expertise in [[Merchant/Legends|business]] to oversee the black market. Due to the planet's significant black market, the Empire maintained a large [[Imperial Office of Customs/Legends|Imperial Customs]] office on the world.''[[The Far Orbit Project]]'' In 0 ABY, the [[Pirate/Legends|pirate]] [[Venslas Beeli]] conducted a number of raids against Brentaal and other worlds in the region, leading the Rebel privateering [[Frigate/Legends|frigate]] ''[[Far Orbit]]'' to [[Battle of the Solar Terrors|attack]] Beeli's pirates.{{WEGCite|story=The Rival|book=The Far Orbit Project}} The ''Far Orbit'' was later lured into a [[Battle in Brentaal space|trap]] by Imperial forces near Brentaal, though it escaped,{{WEGCite|story=The Trap (adventure scenario)|book=The Far Orbit Project}} and some of the ''Far Orbit''{{'s}} crew later [[Mission to Brentaal IV|traveled]] to Brentaal in order to secure a [[Datacard/Legends|datacard]] from an [[Unidentified Rebel waiter|Alliance contact]] and managed to escape [[Imperial Security Bureau/Legends|Imperial Security Bureau]] agents who pursued them.{{WEGCite|story=Raid on Brentaal|book=The Far Orbit Project}} In [[1 ABY/Legends|36:5]], the [[Commission for the Preservation of the New Order/Legends|Commission for the Preservation of the New Order]] moved to place new tariffs on luxury agri-exports from the Bormea sector,{{JournalCite|6|Galaxywide NewsNets}} and the resultant tariffs negatively affected imports to Brentaal.{{JournalCite|3|Galaxywide NewsNets}} Inspired by the popular holo ''[[Kallea's Hope]]'' by [[Neile Janna]], which translated ''The Kallea Cycle'' into a popular and modern format from [[Old Brentaal]] when it was released in 1 ABY, Brentaal's [[Council of Human High Culture]] spent the next two years working on the opera to bring it back to what they called "its classical roots." However, the Council's true goals were the promotion of [[Humanocentrism]], as they reworked the opera to highlight the achievements of Humans and excluded [[Alien/Legends|alien]] performers from the show. On 37:2:23, Imperial Customs uncovered evidence of a [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggling]] scheme that was believed to be responsible for [[Rawmat shortage of 1–2 ABY|redirecting]] raw materials that were intended for Brentaal to the Outer Rim. [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Dalea Trovin]] coordinated the investigation, and Customs raided a warehouse complex in the city of [[Votrad]], discovering thousands of tons of raw materials that had been listed as missing or misrouted. The [[Brentaal Trade News]] published a report on Trovin's efforts, though the captain had not yet been able to determine where the raw materials were being diverted to.{{JournalCite|9|Galaxywide NewsNets}} In [[2 ABY/Legends|2 ABY]] (38:2), Brentaal began preparing for the premiere of ''The Kallea Cycle'', in which [[Vessa Brentioch]] of House Brentioch would portray her ancestor and the famed [[Chandrilan/Legends|Chandrilan]] singer [[Gelod Vothran]] would play Sival Brentioch. The production was performed by the [[Brentaal Hall Conservatory]] and funded by a number of the planet's most prominent houses, including the [[Dajaal Family]], House Brentioch, and [[Hall Jo'uda]], and it took place in [[Votrad Stadium]]—which had been outfitted with more than 100,000 seats and a 500-mete-long stage. [[File:The_Kallea_Cycle.jpg|thumb|left|300px|''The Kallea Cycle''{{'s}} opening night in Votrad Stadium]] The show had a premiere date of 38:2:13, and prominent dignitaries from across the Core Worlds and the Colonies traveled to Brentaal and Votrad in particular to attend, though security remained high to ensure that the production went smoothly. However, the notorious jewel thief [[Tanda Marelle]], known in the [[Media/Legends|media]] as the Tombat, struck at a banquet in Votrad on 38:2:12 that was attended by a number of famous guests; Vessa Brentioch, Gelod Vothran, the production's Maestro [[Trebian Shullos]], Moff [[Jamson Caglio]] of the Bormea sector, [[Imperial Advisor/Legends|Imperial Advisor]] [[Alec Pradeux]], and Inspector [[Zanza Gata]] of the [[Imperial Office of Criminal Investigations/Legends|Imperial Office of Criminal Investigations]] were among the banquest's attendees. However, several of the guests discovered small [[quella stone]]s—the Tombat's trademark—baked in their dessert bowls of [[shim-bay crispa]], an act which many believed to be a statement on Gata's inability to capture the Tombat and one that raised questions as to whether Gata's true intent in overseeing the opera's security was to in fact set a trap for the thief. Moff Caglio publicly expressed his displeasure with the Inspector, but the production of ''The Kallea Cycle'' continued without incident. On 38:4:21, the [[Brentaal League of Guilds]] declared a Landmark Holiday to celebrate a record week of commodities trading, as more credits and stocks had passed through the Brentaal market than ever before during a five-day period. Governor Maclain, House Brentioch, Hall Jo'uda, and the Dajaal Family were among those that benefited from the market activity, which also boosted many corporations in the Core Worlds, and the week-long Landmark Holiday was filled with parades and parties sponsored by the planet's trading houses. The Brentaal Hall Conservatory presented an encore performance of ''The Kallea Cycle'' in celebration before the opera began a tour of the Core Worlds and the Colonies a month later, though Vessa Brentioch was replaced by Neile Janna in the role of Kallea for the [[Kallea Tour]], and the Brentaal commodities exchange was closed during the holiday.{{JournalCite|14|Galaxywide NewsNets}} However, in the weeks after the Landmark Holiday, Brentaal was wrought with scandal: five of the Dajaal Family's commerce officers were arrested after it came to light that they had breached market confidentiality, and the officers claimed that they had passed data to Governor Maclain in exchange for monetary incentives and political favors. Maclain was soon accused of underhanded dealings in the commerce exchange by two of his aides and numerous bureaucrats from nearby systems, and [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] Palpatine himself dispatched Grand Moff [[Rufaan Tigellinus]] to head an investigation of Maclain, leading some to believe that Palpatine had assigned Tigellinus—a member of the exclusive [[Order of the Canted Circle]] and a major player in the politics of the [[Imperial Court/Legends|Imperial Court]]—to the case because Maclain was funding the Rebellion. Tigellinus denied those rumors while assembling his staff for a departure to Brentaal, and he proceeded to interview several bureaucrats in the Bormea and Darpa sectors during his investigation. ===The Battle of Brentaal IV=== {{Quote|For now, though, you must act. Make a stand. Force them to come to you.''"
"''Where?''"
"''It's obvious. Brentaal IV.|Ysanne Isard and Sate Pestage|[[X-Wing Rogue Squadron 21|''X-Wing Rogue Squadron'' 21]]}} [[File:BattleOfBrentaalIV.jpg|thumb|right|250px|New Republic forces attack the Brentaal moonbase.]] Brentaal was still under Imperial control in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], when the Rebel Alliance won the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]] that saw the deaths of both the Emperor and his [[Sith apprentice/Legends|Sith apprentice]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]]. The Empire began to fragment in the wake of the Emperor's death, and the newly-formed [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] began advancing towards the Core Worlds and Coruscant. In 39:12, nine months after the Battle of Endor,''[[Star Wars Omnibus: X-Wing Rogue Squadron Volume 3]]'' the elite New Republic [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] unit [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Squadron]] was sent to recon Brentaal, and a group of five fighters entered the Brentaal system and began to collect data. By that time, the Empire had established a [[Brentaal Moonbase|moonbase]] on the surface of one of Brentaal's moons and placed the Imperial [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Lon Isoto]] in command of the planet's military forces, and Imperial [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE fighters]] were deployed to drive off the intruders. The New Republic fighters emerged victorious and damaged the moonbase's interior before departing the system. [[Grand Vizier/Legends|Grand Vizier]] [[Sate Pestage/Legends|Sate Pestage]] had assumed control of the Empire after Palpatine's death, but [[Director/Legends|Director]] [[Ysanne Isard]] of [[Imperial Intelligence/Legends|Imperial Intelligence]] desired the throne herself and advanced her cause by serving as a mediator in his dealings with [[Imperial Ruling Council/Legends#After Endor: Sate Pestage and the Cabal|the Cabal]]—a group of wealthy and politically influential citizens—and playing the two groups against each other. Isard advised Pestage to invite an attack on Brentaal, believing that she could orchestrate a New Republic victory there and bring about Pestage's downfall. As Admiral Isoto was considered incompetent, Isard sent part of the elite [[181st Imperial Fighter Wing/Legends|181st Imperial Fighter Wing]] under [[Colonel/Legends|Colonel]] [[Baron/Legends|Baron]] [[Soontir Fel/Legends|Soontir Fel]] to Brentaal, and Pestage agreed to her suggestion before issuing a public statement that the Empire would defend Brentaal from invasion. In response, Admiral [[Gial Ackbar/Legends|Gial Ackbar]] of the New Republic began active preparations for conquering the planet, giving Rogue Squadron and Colonel [[Horton Salm/Legends|Horton Salm's]] [[Aggressor Wing]] two [[Standard week/Legends|weeks]] to prepare. As planned, two weeks later a [[New Republic task force (Brentaal IV)|task force]] under Ackbar's command entered the Brentaal system and attacked the planet's moonbase, capturing the facility and using it as a staging ground for an assault on Brentaal itself. The Imperial forces under Isoto's command made no attempt to retake or destroy the facility, though the admiral—who spent most of his days in with pleasure girls in the city of [[Vuultin]]—ordered the razing of the forests around the city in order to install missile sites and a bunker for Fel's 18st. Though the locals protested, Isoto ignored them, believing that his presence in Vuultin made the strategically-worthless city a prime target for the New Republic. Fel disagreed and sent most of his forces to nearby [[Oradin]], as the city's spaceport facilities would aid the New Republic in landing troops on the surface. Fel was correct: Admiral Ackbar ordered Rogue Squadron to feint at Vuultin while Aggressor Wing accompanied their main forces to Oradin. [[File:Battle_of_Brentaal_by_Bruno_Werneck.jpg|thumb|left|300px|The Battle of Brentaal]] When Rogue Squadron and the 181st began to [[Starfighter combat/Legends|dogfight]] among the skyscrapers of Vuultin, Isoto decided to pull his capital ships back to the night side of the planet. Baron Fel's fighters inflicted heavy losses on Aggressor Wing in the first minutes of the battle, but the panicked admiral demanded that Fel pull his fighters back to Vuultin and defend him, and the New Republic command ordered Rogue Squadron to withdraw in fear that the 181st would attack the main battle group. Oradin was heavily damaged but was captured by the New Republic, though Fel's second-in-command [[Turr Phennir/Legends|Turr Phennir]] took out a New Republic assault shuttle that crashed into a Brentaal school, injuring a large number of children. When Fel refused a medal for his actions, Isoto decided to declare a Brentaalan holiday entitled "Fel's Day," and despite the desires of both the Cabal and Pestage, Isard's manipulations kept the two sides from knowing that they both thought Isoto should be relieved of command. When news of Oradin's fall reached Coruscant, Isard ordered a [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] of two hundred and five vessels to launch from Coruscant and head to Brentaal with the purpose of evacuating the planet's wealthy upper classes.[[X-Wing Rogue Squadron 23|''X-Wing Rogue Squadron'' 23]] By doing so, Isard hoped to make Pestage look foolish and deprive the Cabal of a potential power base.[[X-Wing Rogue Squadron 24|''X-Wing Rogue Squadron'' 24]] When the fleet arrived at Brentaal, the [[New Republic Provisional Council]] feared that the evacuation would mean the removal of Brentaal's wealth and cultural artifacts and as such ordered the New Republic forces to stop the evacuation. Rogue Squadron and Aggressor Wing worked to disable the evacuating ships over Vuultin while assault transports landed to capture the city, and Baron Fel—angry that Isard's manipulations had endangered his pilots—led his unit against Rogue Squadron in order to follow his orders and honor his duty. During the assault, Isoto was [[Assassin/Legends|assassinated]] by his concubine [[Grania (Brentaali)|Grania]] at Isard's orders after he complied with Isard's demand for him to issue an evacuation order. With the issuing of the evacuation order, every ship on Brentaal was given immediate clearance for vertical takeoff, but Fel was forced to order the 181st to retreat from the battle and protect the fleeing citizens. ===Later history=== {{Quote|The treasonous people whose plotting allowed the Rebels to take Brentaal IV died for their perfidy. I welcome you, the loyal survivors, with the promise that your suffering—|Part of Sate Pestage's address to the evacuated Brentaalans|}} [[File:BrentaalPlanet.jpg|thumb|250px|Brentaal IV]] The Brentaalans who managed to evacuate were welcomed to Coruscant by Pestage, who publicly blamed the loss of the [[Battle of Brentaal IV (Galactic Civil War)|Battle of Brentaal IV]] on treasonous citizens who had died in the conflict. From Brentaal, the New Republic moved their forces up the Hydian Way in [[6 ABY/Legends|6 ABY]] after conquering much of the western and southern galaxy, and Oradin had been rebuilt to its former bustling state by the year [[9 ABY/Legends|9 ABY]], when the [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droids]] [[Whistler]] and [[R5-G8/Legends|Gate]]—the [[Droid/Legends|droids]] of New Republic [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]] [[Corran Horn/Legends|Corran Horn]] and [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]]—traveled on a solo mission to the city in order to locate the smugglers [[Talon Karrde]] and [[Mirax Terrik Horn|Mirax Terrik]]. The [[Grand Oradin Hotel]] was a major resort in the city, and the building's [[Turbolift/Legends|turbolifts]] played recordings of the history of the Battle of Brentaal IV to their passengers. The planet was briefly [[Battle of Brentaal (10 ABY)|conquered]] by Grand Moff [[Ardus Kaine]] in [[10 ABY/Legends|10 ABY]] during the offensive planned by the reborn Emperor Palpatine. Brentaal remained a part of the New Republic for the next decade and a half, and the [[Brentaal Academy]] hosted the 412th [[Proceedings of Galactic Anthropology and History]], with the [[Historian/Legends|historian]] [[Vilnau Teupt]] as the keynote speaker in [[24 ABY/Legends|24 ABY]]. During the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]] of [[25 ABY/Legends|25]]–[[29 ABY/Legends|29 ABY]], Brentaal was [[Battle of Brentaal IV (Yuuzhan Vong War)|attacked]] by the extragalactic [[Yuuzhan Vong]] [[Species/Legends|species]], and like those of Ralltiir and Chandrila, the planet's inhabitants chose to fight the invaders, though several of the planet's cities were destroyed when the Brentaalans fought the Yuuzhan Vong. ==Inhabitants== {{Quote|I'm just tired of living on Brentaal. Everyone seems to care only about making millions of credits, scoring big trade deals, scheduling the most profitable cargo runs, and cashing in on the latest commerce trends.|[[Darrik]]|''[[Imperial Double-Cross]]''}} [[File:Evac.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The wealthy of Brentaal attempt to flee the planet during the Battle of Brentaal.]] Brentaal's society was focused entirely around commerce, with the hundreds of Brentaal Houses controlling the planetary economy and political environment. On Brentaal, politics were a means to advance one's interests in the commercial world, not a way to gain power, and the planet was ruled by a participatory democracy. Representatives of each Brentaal House met daily in the central [[Trade Hall]] in Cormond, where they made public policy and coaxed the economy in desired directions. The Houses, which were connected by thousands of intricate alliances and factions, were nearly all organized by family, as the ability to own a controlling stake in a Brentaal guild or House was originally restricted to family members and family-controlled businesses. A complex system involving permits and exchanges of massive numbers of credits later opened access to some foreigners limited access to certain Houses. [[House Kallea|Houses Kallea]], Brentioch and [[House Okeefe|Okeefe]], Hall Ju'oda, and the Dajaal Family were among the more successful and influential Houses on Brentaal. With a population of approximately 65 billion, Brentaal was primarily populated by Humans, as they made up 88% of the planet's inhabitants, and the planet's primary language was [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Galactic Basic Standard]]. The popular Brentaalan folkhero was one who fearlessly trail-blazes new hyperspace routes as a spacefaring merchant, and Freia Kallea became a legendary figure in Brentaalan society for doing just that. Many major megacorporations maintained their headquarters on Brentaal, particularly in the capital of Cormond, and the planet also had a very well-regarded cuisine that was the result of thousands of years of interaction with other cultures. The architecture of Brentaal's cities was functional and stark as befitted a culture based on commerce, but as the Brentaalans favored organic-looking architecture, many offworlders considered their buildings to be oddly beautiful. As a result of its position at the junction of the Hydian and the Perlemian, Brentaal was home to many shipping companies and also had a thriving criminal underworld and black market. ==Locations== {{Quote|This world has so much to offer, Fel, you should partake of its treasures before the Rebels unleash their wrath.|Lon Isoto|}} [[File:Vuultin.jpg|thumb|left|300px|The city of Vuultin]] Brentaal's inhabitants lived primarily in cities that were primarily filled with spaceports, trade markets, financial markets, industrial centers, and warehouses. The city of Votrad was home to the [[Votrad Independent Downport]], an enormous spaceport, and the [[Votrad Stadium]], which was large enough to hold 100,000 patrons. The Brentaal Academy and the [[Brentaal Commerce Academy]] were two learning institutions on the world; the Commerce Academy trained children for the planet's commerce-focused society, with some courses including advanced stock tracking, distribution theory, and speculative investing. While the planet's equatorial regions, plateaus, and flatlands were dominated by the commercial starports and warehouses essential to Brentaal's commercial society, the planet's polar regions were primarily devoted to recreational pursuits. Brentaal's capital, Cormond, lay on the coast of the [[Suporro Sea]] near the [[Gravaal mountain range|Gravaal Mountains]], and it was home to the Trade Hall—the center of Brentaal's commercial interests and the seat of government. The Trade Hall featured a number of expansive trade floors, thousands of offices, gardens, and shipping centers, in addition to a private spaceport. While the rest of Brentaal was largely devoted to handling cargo, Cormond was responsible for directing the commerce as a result of the presence of the Trade Hall. The city of Oradin was located on a coast and was home to an [[Imperial-class spaceport]], making it far more strategically valuable than the large city of Vuultin, which was located to the west in a forest and lacked a [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceport]]. Oradin was home to dozens of resorts and hotels, ranging in size from tiny hovels to the large upscale luxury of the [[Grand Oradin Hotel]], which was known as the Grand Imperial Hotel in the years before the Battle of Brentaal IV during the Galactic Civil War. [[File:BrentaalsFavisResort.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The Favis Resort]] The [[Curovao family]], which ran the shipping company [[Curovao ImpEx]], lent its name to the city of [[Curovao]], though [[Simith Gorofila]], head of the so-called [[Brentaal Dissidents League]], accused the family and the city of corrupt dealings with the Republic. The [[Favis Resort]] was an artificial island anchored in Brentaal's mild south polar sea, and it was one of the resort communities where Brentaalan nobles and guild officers retired to when the planet's heat became oppressive during summertime in the southern hemisphere. Numerous casinos, luxury hotels, and sports stadiums could be found at the Resort, and yacht regattas and glacier-climbing expeditions were conducted regularly. However, the Favis Resort also had a reputation for being the site of corporate espionage, as Brentaalan merchants rarely ever left their work behind while on vacation. ==Behind the scenes== Brentaal IV was first mentioned in the "[[Galaxywide NewsNets]]" segment of [[Star Wars Adventure Journal 3|''Star Wars Adventure Journal'' 3]], published in [[1994]], and it received mentions in a number of sources and roleplaying guides in the years that followed. The planet first appeared in the roleplaying adventure ''[[Imperial Double-Cross]]'' in [[1997]], and the [[Star Wars: X-Wing Rogue Squadron: In the Empire's Service|''In the Empire's Service'']] story arc of the ''[[Star Wars: X-Wing Rogue Squadron]]'' comic series was focused on Brentaal a few months later. The roleplaying adventure ''[[The Far Orbit Project]]'', published in [[1998]], stated that Brentaal lacked moons, despite the ''X-wing'' comics less than a year earlier clearly depicting Brentaal possessing at least one moon with a military base on it, and all subsequent sources and appearances have stated that Brentaal IV has two moons. ==Appearances== {{ScrollBox|content=
